production.note: Calendar years 2006-2010 (owner decision, 8 October 2026; home-market record). Classic.com: 'Introduced in 2006', 'was replaced in 2010 by the Agera', 'Only 48 CCX cars were built, including its variants'. The CCX was also sold in the US: Classic.com says it 'was modified externally and mechanically to meet U.S. regulations'; US model years were not sourced, so the owner chose the home market. The CCXR and CCX Edition are separate variants.

body.note: Koenigsegg: 'Two-door, two-seater with detachable hardtop roof' (removable roof panel, recorded as Coupe like the Agera R and One:1).

configuration.note: Koenigsegg: 'Koenigsegg aluminium V8, 4 valves per cylinder, double overhead camshafts'.

aspiration.note: Koenigsegg: 'Twin Rotrex centrifugal superchargers with response system', '1.4 bar boost pressure'.

fuel.note: Koenigsegg: 'Sequential, multipoint fuel injection'; petrol V8, inferred.

drivetrain.note: Classic.com: power went 'to the rear wheels'.

transmission.note: Koenigsegg: 'Specially developed transversal 6-speed gearbox, with optional paddle-shift'. Classic.com: 'a 6-speed manual or sequential gearbox' (classic-com-ccx). The paddle-shift sequential option is an automated manual.

powerHp.note: Quote (Koenigsegg technical specifications): "Power output: 806 Bhp at 7000 rpm". Stored as published (powerStandard Other, as for the Agera R); no kW or PS figure was on the page. Classic.com also says 806hp.

weightLb.note: Step 4 (manufacturer dry weight): no manufacturer or magazine-panel curb weight was found. Quote (Koenigsegg technical specifications): "Dry weight: 1280 kg (2821 lbs)". 1,280 kg x 2.20462 = 2,821.9, rounded to 2,822 lb (Koenigsegg prints 2,821 lbs).
